exposure: caesarean section in the index pregnancy
cohort: 48 patients who underwent emergency obstetric hysterectomy out of 6809 deliveries at a tertiary care hospital, majority of whom were multiparous women aged 20-35 years.
finding: The most common indication for emergency obstetric hysterectomy was uterine atony (50%), followed by morbidly adherent placenta (45.81%), and the study found associations with previous caesarean sections, lack of antenatal care, and deliveries at inappropriate settings.
